leaf_surface_top.label: Leaf Surface: Top

definitions.joint_ig: IG(Y;F1,F2) for the joint value-set cell. Upper bound on what the pair can contribute and the basis for the synergy test.
definitions.conditional_ig: IG of one feature given the other = joint_IG - IG(other). The incremental information the second feature adds after the first; zero means the first already contains it.
definitions.synergy: joint_IG - max(single_IG). Positive means the pair is worth more than its best member alone; zero or negative means redundancy, and the pair should not drive observation design.
definitions.redundancy: IG(F1) + IG(F2) - joint_IG. Bits the two features share; high redundancy means they are proxies for the same distinction.
definitions.probe_candidate_set: Candidate set when a single observed value is queried, averaged over the species' asserted values. Multi-valued Dirr rows make the exact cell look more specific than any real observation: a species asserting {Ovate, Elliptic} is alone in its exact cell but every single-value probe still returns the full Ovate group.

bark.dirr_note: The Dirr extracted vocabulary has no bark feature (no value column maps to bark). Leaf x bark fusion is therefore not testable from the current Dirr parquets; it would need a new Dirr bark extraction or a GoBotany crossover that keeps provenance separate.

gobotany.access: GoBotany parquet tables read directly (gobotany_taxon, gobotany_taxon_character_value, gobotany_character_value_label); the pile-scoped GoBotanyDevoAdapter query layer is not used.
gobotany.provenance_note: GoBotany is used only to assess coverage and resolve conflicts. Its labels are never merged into the Dirr feature table.

metric_definitions.coverage: Fraction of the candidate species for which the source asserts any value. A feature the guide does not document cannot key those species out, so coverage bounds every other metric.
metric_definitions.information_gain: IG(Y;F) = H(Y) - H(Y|F), in bits. How many bits of species identity the feature removes from a uniform species prior. Directly comparable to the log2(candidate-set) reduction and independent of feature alphabet size (unlike raw entropy of F).
metric_definitions.nmi: IG / sqrt(H(F) * H(Y)). Symmetric normalization so a feature with a large or small alphabet can be compared on a 0..1 scale; 1.0 means the feature partition determines species identity exactly.
metric_definitions.conditional_entropy: H(Y|F), in bits, and as a ratio of H(Y). The residual species uncertainty after reading the feature; the ratio is the share of the prior that survives, so lower is better and it is scale-free.
metric_definitions.unique_resolution: Fraction of species that end up alone in their feature cell. This is the operational question -- can this feature by itself name the species? Reported over covered species (fair to sparse features) and over all species (deployment-honest, unobserved = unresolved).
metric_definitions.median_candidate_set: Median number of species sharing a species' feature cell. The candidate set the next feature has to split. Median rather than mean because a few huge cells (e.g. all simple-leaved species) dominate the mean.
metric_definitions.probe_candidate_set: Candidate set when a single observed value is queried, averaged over the species' asserted values. Multi-valued Dirr rows make the exact cell look more specific than any real observation: a species asserting {Ovate, Elliptic} is alone in its exact cell but every single-value probe still returns the full Ovate group.
metric_definitions.probe_information_gain: IG under the single-observation model: each species' weight is split evenly over its asserted values, so the metric measures what ONE observed value tells you. This is the primary ranking key because the pipeline sees a single value at a time; the exact asserted-set IG is kept as the guide's upper bound. Where Dirr's values are co-observable (colour + lustre + indumentum in leaf_surface_top), probe IG is a conservative lower bound: a real observer can report several tags.
metric_definitions.image_weighted: The same metrics with each species weighted by its LeafSnap image count. Secondary only: it says what the dataset emphasises, not what the field guide can discriminate. Reported to expose the difference, never used for ranking.
metric_definitions.joint_ig: IG(Y;F1,F2) for the joint value-set cell. Upper bound on what the pair can contribute and the basis for the synergy test.
metric_definitions.conditional_ig: IG of one feature given the other = joint_IG - IG(other). The incremental information the second feature adds after the first; zero means the first already contains it.
metric_definitions.synergy: joint_IG - max(single_IG). Positive means the pair is worth more than its best member alone; zero or negative means redundancy, and the pair should not drive observation design.
metric_definitions.redundancy: IG(F1) + IG(F2) - joint_IG. Bits the two features share; high redundancy means they are proxies for the same distinction.

warnings.text: Joint features MUST be fused across observations / spatial tracks. A same-view pair can share one crop; a non-local pair (leaf obverse vs leaf reverse, leaf vs whole plant, leaf vs flower) cannot. Never assume a non-local pair is visible in one image, and never train a single-crop model to predict both sides of one.

An absent Dirr assertion is a documentation gap, not a biological value. Entropy treats it as its own cell and the deployment candidate set falls back to the full space, so sparse features are penalised rather than flattered.

Exact-value-set cells overstate resolution for multi-valued features. Compare resolution_rate_* with probe_* rates; the probe numbers describe what a single observed value returns. For features whose values are co-observable (colour + lustre + indumentum), the probe is a lower bound rather than a point estimate; the exact set is the upper bound. The truth sits between them and only the imaging model can settle it.
Pairs and triples with few shared species are noisy; n_shared is reported beside every joint metric. Underpowered spotlights are labelled rather than ranked.
LeafSnap image counts are lab-heavy and species-unbalanced. Image-weighted metrics are secondary context only.
Dirr is the primary vocabulary. GoBotany values appear only in the coverage/conflict check, are labelled by source, and are never merged into the Dirr assertions.
